samples.text:
The line graph shows how the population of Marlow City changed from 1950 to 2020 and the table show the different kinds of housing in the city in 1950 and 2020.

Overall, the population increased a lot during the period and the most common type of housing changed from terraced houses to apartments.

In 1950 the population of the city was 0.4 million. It rised to 0.6 million in 1960 and 0.9 million in 1970. Then it continued to grow to 1.2 million in 1980 and 1.3 million in 1990, which was a slow increase. After that the population grew more quickly, it reached 1.9 million in 2010 and 2.4 million in 2020. This means the population was six times bigger at the end.

Looking at the table, in 1950 terraced houses was the biggest type with 61%, but in 2020 it fell to 24%. On the other hand, apartments increased from 12% to 58%. Detached houses decreased from 18% to 11% and other type of housing went down slightly from 9% to 7%.
samples.why: Simple but relevant overview · all main features covered, though the population data is listed year by year · adequate linking · limited vocabulary (increased, grew) · errors in verb forms, agreement and punctuation.

samples.text:
The line graph illustrates the growth in Marlow City's population over seventy-year period starting in 1950, while the table compares the proportions of different housing types in the first and last years.

It is clear that the city's population rose continuously, increasing sixfold overall. At the same time, the housing stock shifted markedly from terraced houses towards apartments, which became the dominant type by 2020.

In 1950, Marlow City had 0.4 million residents. This number climbed steadily to 1.2 million by 1980, but growth then slowed considerably, with the population reaching only 1.3 million in 1990. From that point on, the increase accelerated again, to 1.5 million in 2000 and 1.9 million in 2010, before peaking at 2.4 million in 2020.

As for housing, terraced houses made up 61% of homes in 1950, yet their share had fallen to 24% by 2020. Apartments showed the opposite pattern, rising from just 12% to 58%, which is almost five times as much. Detached houses became less common, dropping from 18% to 11%, whereas the other category remain relatively stable at 9% and 7% respectively.
samples.why: Clear overview of both visuals · key stages of growth identified rather than listed · good cohesion (From that point on, As for) · some less common vocabulary · occasional minor errors.

samples.text:
The line graph charts the population of Marlow City from 1950 to 2020, and the accompanying table shows how the composition of its housing stock changed between the start and end of that period.

The most striking features are the city's sustained population growth, with the number of residents multiplying six times over, and a fundamental shift in housing from terraced houses to apartments.

Marlow City's population stood at 0.4 million in 1950 and grew at a fairly steady pace to 1.2 million by 1980, tripling in thirty years. The following decade saw only marginal growth, to 1.3 million, but expansion resumed thereafter and gathered pace after 2000, so that the city was home to 2.4 million people by 2020.

This growth coincided with a transformation in the type of homes available. In 1950, terraced houses accounted for 61% of the housing stock, around five times the proportion of apartments (12%). By 2020, however, the positions had been reversed: apartments comprised 58% of homes, while the share of terraced houses had shrunk to 24%. Detached houses also became less prevalent, falling from 18% to 11%, and other types of accommodation changed little, edging down from 9% to 7%.
samples.why: Well-selected key features and a clear overview · the two visuals linked naturally · accurate figures and derived comparisons · precise vocabulary (marginal, prevalent, composition) · wide range of error-free structures.
